set.reason: The hundredths-to-decimal correspondence is directly used in percent/decimal conversion. Only that conversion component is required, not every fraction/decimal conversion exercise.
set.scope: percent to decimal and back via hundredths

set.reason: Writing a percent as hundredths uses what the percent sign means as a relative quantity per hundred.
set.scope: converting between percents, fractions and decimals

set.reason: The stated criterion allows decimal or fraction conversion before multiplying. Decimal multiplication satisfies it without the fraction multiplication procedure. Gemini makes the optional fraction representation universal; the analogous fraction-of model is useful preparation only.
set.scope: Fraction-of-a-quantity modeling as preparation for percent-of calculations

set.reason: The criterion explicitly first converts the percent to a decimal or fraction and then multiplies; the conversion is therefore a required step in this stated procedure.
set.scope: converting the percent before multiplying

set.reason: Knowing the forward calculation helps interpret the inverse problem, but an equal-sharing unitary argument can find one percent and then the whole directly. The percent-of procedure is not itself necessary for the division criterion, contrary to the Gemini upgrade.
set.scope: The forward whole-times-rate relation as preparation for finding an unknown whole

set.reason: The target explicitly requires choosing division to find unit 1. This is the same unit-whole division relation named by the prerequisite criterion, even when the rate is expressed as a decimal. A pure equation solution that never supplies this division interpretation misses that explicit criterion. Require the shared relation, not general fraction-division fluency.
set.scope: Identifying the unknown unit whole and dividing its known part by the corresponding rate
